title: IIS, feasibility relaxation and several objectives in gurobipy

questions.stem: A scenario forces project P9 in by setting the lower bound of its binary x_P9 to 1. The model is infeasible; computeIIS marks only the rows budget_2029 and must_P4, with IISMinimal 1. May the team conclude that forcing P9 in plays no part?

options.text: Yes, since an IIS lists every rule the conflict depends on
options.says: Gurobi never puts a binary's bounds in an IIS, so a conflict that needs the forced bound could not name it.

options.text: Yes, since IISMinimal 1 shows the binary's bound was tested and dropped
options.says: IISMinimal says the set returned is irreducible; it says nothing about bounds Gurobi never considers.

options.text: No, since computeIIS reads no bounds of any kind, binary or not
options.says: IISLB and IISUB mark bounds of other variables; only binary bounds are left out.

options.text: No, since a binary's bounds never take part in Gurobi's IIS
options.says: Right: the variable attribute page says so; write the forcing as a named row to see it in an IIS.

origin.section: computeIIS Names the Rows That Clash

questions.stem: A must-do row (x_P4 summed over its start years = 1) clashes with a budget row that would need $500k more. The team runs feasRelaxS(0, False, False, True) on a copy and optimizes. What repair comes back?

options.text: The must-do row breaks by 1, since that is the least total violation
options.says: Right: with every row at penalty 1, one unit on the must-do row is cheaper than 500 on the budget, as ArtP_must_P017 = 1 showed.

options.text: The budget row breaks by 500, since budgets are relaxed before rules
options.says: feasRelaxS treats every row alike at penalty 1; it dropped must_P017 rather than add $310k.

options.text: Both rows break, since each row in the conflict must give a little
options.says: The relaxation minimizes the total violation; one row breaking was enough in every run of the lesson.

options.text: No repair, since feasRelaxS only relaxes variable bounds
options.says: Its last argument, crelax=True, lets every row be violated; vrelax is the one for bounds.

origin.section: feasRelax Repairs the Model, and the Penalties Decide What Gives

questions.stem: A MathOpt model has NPV as its primary objective (priority 0) and spend as an auxiliary objective with priority 1. A colleague ports it to gurobipy with setObjectiveN(npv, 0, priority=0) and setObjectiveN(spend, 1, priority=1, weight=-1). Which objective does Gurobi optimize first?

options.text: NPV, since objective index 0 always comes first
options.says: The index only numbers the objectives; the priority sets the order.

options.text: NPV, since priorities keep their order between the two APIs
options.says: MathOpt runs the lowest priority number first, Gurobi the highest, so the order flips.

options.text: Spend, since Gurobi runs the highest priority value first
options.says: Right: in gurobipy larger priorities go first, the opposite of MathOpt; swap them to keep NPV first.

options.text: Neither, since Gurobi blends both into one weighted sum
options.says: Only objectives with equal priority are blended; 0 and 1 are solved in separate passes.

origin.section: setObjectiveN Solves Objectives by Priority, Highest First
